newsitem.title: UK: Safrica central bank to reduce c/a deficit-Stals.
newsitem.headline: Safrica central bank to reduce c/a deficit-Stals.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said that after the slide of the rand in recent months, the bank has given priority to reducing the large current account deficit.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television in London Stals said the rand's slide since February this year was "motivated more by policy perceptions of developments in South Africa."
"It is accepted that the increase in interest rates of one percent will not resolve this kind of problem," he said.
The inflows of "short-term speculative capital" late last year and early this year had turned around on political rather than economic perceptions and had flowed out again.

"The situation has stabilised in the meantime but we have a substantial deficit on the current account of the balance of payments...policy priority has shifted to correcting the current account deficit," he added. The deficit had been caused by a substantial increase in imports over the last 18 months. It would "take time to make the necessary adjustments".

"The Reserve Bank is quite prepared to provide assistance to the foreign exchange markets,to use our reserves by intervention in the forward foreign exchange market and make use of available credit facilities of the Bank at this stage," he said.

Asked what had happened to the lifting of foreign exchange controls, Stals denied it was "on the back burner". "I wouldn't say it was on the back burner but we have to be more cautious because of the vulnerable balance of payments situation."

"The exchange control relaxation programme is a structural adjustment which I believe must go ahead in the next six to nine months. There are administrative arrangements which can be relaxed and we will continue with the programme."
